text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO: P1 - eu-west-1 (az3) intermittent egress failures detected by perf-prober. Error spike for external API calls from customer-facing endpoints. Paging @jamie (sre-oncall) and @ryan (networking)
jamie: saw it. getting context. is this affecting all regions or just eu-west-1?
ryan: looks localized to AZ3 in eu-west-1. traceroutes show traffic exiting to the VPC peer instead of the NAT gateway for a subset of subnets.
maria: any terraform run recently that touched route tables or peering?
eli: support reports 3 customers with 502/timeout errors beginning ~12:05 UTC. I've opened customer tickets and warned them we're investigating.
jamie: ack. @devops-bot can you post current route table for vpc-0a1b2c? paste below
devops-bot: ```
RouteTable rtb-0a1b2c
  10.0.0.0/16 local
  0.0.0.0/0 vpc-peering-08aa (propagated=false)  <-- suspicious
  10.1.0.0/24 nat-0f1e2d3c
``` 
ryan: that 0.0.0.0/0 to peering is wrong. should point to nat gateway. I think a terraform change earlier appended a default route to the peering route table and an apply targeted the wrong RT in AZ3.
maria: who ran the apply? iam logs show user: infra-ci (automation) 11:58 UTC, target: rtb-0a1b2c
jamie: mitigation plan: 1) replace the default route in rtb-0a1b2c to point to nat-0f1e2d3c 2) create temporary explicit allow NACL for outbound 443 from problematic subnets 3) failover traffic to standby NAT in az3 if needed 4) keep customers updated. executing step 1 now.
ryan: i'll watch BGP/peering metrics and ensure no flaps when we change route.
jamie: running:
```bash
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0f1e2d3c
``` 
jamie: done. route replaced. devops-bot confirm?
devops-bot: route replace succeeded for rtb-0a1b2c -> nat-0f1e2d3c
eli: customers reporting partial recovery, one still seeing timeouts.
ryan: let's check the NAT health for nat-0f1e2d3c and conntrack. metrics show CPU spike and conntrack table near capacity in az3.
maria: can we spin a new nat in az3 and attach? avoid changing existing NAT if conntrack full.
jamie: provisioning nat-standby-az3 now. ETA ~3m.
devops-bot: NAT nat-standby-az3 created and associated with subnet-az3-public.
jamie: updating route table to point to standby NAT to drain connections off the overloaded one.
```bash
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-standby-az3
```
jamie: route update done.
ryan: monitoring egress success rate... 200-> 95% success, errors trending down. conntrack freed up on previous NAT.
eli: all three affected customers confirm restored for majority of traffic, one reports intermittent 502s still but improving.
support-liaison: posting status update to customers: "We're seeing partial recovery; network team replaced a misapplied default route and failed over to standby NAT. We're continuing to monitor."
jamie: handoff: I'm paging @ryan to take lead for next 30m to monitor for regressions and bha (business hours) impact. I'll go to follow-up and prepare incident record.
ryan: taking lead. setting local watch and synthetic checks to aggressive 15s cadence for 30m.
maria: assign follow-ups: 1) postmortem to include terraform guardrail to prevent global 0.0.0.0/0 on peering RTs 2) alert when conntrack > 70% 3) add route-table tagging check in CI. I'll file tickets.
eli: escalations done. customers also asked for RCA; will sync with you all when postmortem draft is ready.
jamie: adding notes: probable root cause = automation (infra-ci) terraform apply targeted rtb-0a1b2c in az3 which had a propagated peering entry; automation lacked a safeguard that prevents default route to peering in prod.
ryan: long-term mitigation: add policy to prevent route propagation to peering for default routes, and a deny rule in terraform module for destination_cidr_block = 0.0.0.0/0 on peering route tables.
jamie: incident severity downgraded to P2 at 12:33 UTC; monitoring period continues. closing pager for on-call but keeping thread open for handoff.
eli: thanks team. :white_check_mark: I'll update customers with timeline and next steps once postmortem ticket is created.
support-liaison: logging customer impact: 3 customers, peak impact 8m, errors spike to 40% for affected egress paths.
jamie: final check: all synthetic checks green for 10m. handing off to @ryan. I'll update incident document and assign to root-cause squad.
ryan: ack. continuing watch. assigning postmortem owner: @maria
devops-bot: Incident closed (automated) - status: mitigated. Links: runbook/incident/1779991234
jamie: thanks everyone. follow-ups: terraform guardrails, conntrack alerts, tagging and CI checks. I'll draft the timeline.
eli: marking customer tickets resolved pending postmortem.
